objective: The coordinator's go-ahead of 2026-11-26 on the first direction of the report that delivered Chapter 11 of the guide: a measure of how much of a change arrives, the half of the owner's lamp that lesson 11.4 calls untested. Change one start in one place and count, round by round, the share of the births that differ, against the number of knots made that round, in growths of known dimension under the ordinary count first, then in the supplied settings in which a change was heard between patterns. Stop when each setting is read as weakening (the share falls as one over the round's count, or faster), holding (a positive share), or taking over (the share goes to one).
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (referee pending; corrected before the referee): under the ordinary count, by descent, a change at a start re-makes every birth of the changed knot's line and none of the other's, so no weakening of the lamp's kind is found; read without names a dimension-two growth forgets its start (two unrelated starts differ in no birth from round 4), and seven changes at the start show only as a fixed 4, 5 or 1 births a round; other changes hold or take over; a struck pulse is never undone; between two patterns nothing falls with the steps.
title: How much of a change arrives: the share of a growth's births that a single change alters, round by round
